label: Groovy autonomy
title: A Groovy field can have its own rule, but Rule 110's does not
summary: A three-site periodic witness proves that Rule 110's entire original Groovy field cannot determine its next field. The known Rule-32 G-to-Rule128 factor remains an exact positive example.
takeaway: Autonomy requires retaining every distinction that can affect the next observation; looking farther away cannot restore a distinction erased from the entire field.
